theorem n04bActualTypedAtlas_moving_negative_reference_unitPoint
    {D : ReferenceData} {T : MaterialData} {S : PhysicalSpacesData}
    {C : NonlinearGeometryData S} {R : ReturnEquationData S}
    {L : ReturnCorrectionData S} {base loss : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hT : IsMaterialData D T) (hS : IsPhysicalSpaces D T S)
    (hN : NonlinearPropertiesThrough03 D T S C R L base loss ε)
    (hfield : N04bFieldRegularity D S C L base ε)
    (e : ℕ ≃ N04PieceIndex D) (z : AnnularState S × ℝ)
    (m : ℕ) (side : Bool) (p : PolarPoint) :
    let K := n04bActualTypedAtlas hT hS hN hfield e
    p ∈ physicalPieceOpen S K z (e.symm (.inl (m, side))) →
      p ∈ Ioo (C.left m) (C.right m) ×ˢ (univ : Set ℝ) ∧
      (p.1 = n04bActualReferenceCut hN m ∨
        ∃ refSide : Bool,
          (if refSide then n04bActualReferenceCut hN m < p.1
            else p.1 < n04bActualReferenceCut hN m) ∧
          let j := e.symm (.inl (m, refSide))
          let q := n07aCanonicalUnitInversePoint (n07aPhysicalIntervalData K) j p
          p ∈ referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K j ∧
            q ∈ CanonicalGeometry.unitStrip ∧
            CanonicalGeometry.physicalUnitPoint K j q = p)

proof_review.step: One original actual atlas and actual moving input
proof_review.detail: K is introduced from the theorem's literal let n04bActualTypedAtlas hT hS hN hfield e. The input is physicalPieceOpen S K z at e.symm(.inl(m,side)). Unfolding only the project constructor and applying n04bTypedAtlasData_physicalPieceOpen, followed by Equiv.apply_symm_apply, produces the genuine current typed domain at the same z,C,L,m,side.

proof_review.step: Actual moving half is contained in the original component
proof_review.detail: n04b_typed_negative_domain_subset has exactly the required subset header and no regularity, material, neighborhood or chart-invertibility premise. Its proof takes the original-domain conjunct of mem_n04bTravelDomain. The candidate therefore legitimately proves p in Ioo(C.left m)(C.right m)×univ for arbitrary z admitted by its input.

proof_review.step: Equality to the old optical cut remains a separate outcome
proof_review.detail: The by_cases split uses precisely n04bActualReferenceCut hN m. When equality holds, Or.inl closes that branch without claiming reference open-half membership at the cut. This is the old reference cut, not the current moving cut.

proof_review.step: Reference-side selection retains the same m
proof_review.detail: Off the cut, lt_or_gt_of_ne gives p.1<cut or cut<p.1. false yields the strict interval(C.left m,cut), true yields(cut,C.right m). The definitions n04bNegativeLeft/right reduce with these concrete Boolean constructors, and hfull supplies the remaining strict endpoint. The exact API pattern is already used in the fully read N04bReferenceHalves.n04b_negativeHalf_existsUnique.

proof_review.step: Reference metadata, enumeration and point are exact
proof_review.detail: n04bTypedAtlasData_referencePhysicalPieceOpen reduces to Ioo(n04bReferenceTypedLeft...)(n04bReferenceTypedRight...)×univ. Applying e to e.symm(.inl(m,refSide)) and unfolding the two reference typed endpoint definitions gives exactly the preceding hr. No new e, component, chart, C/R/L object, cell or material sample is selected.

proof_review.step: Width positivity is derived, not assumed
proof_review.detail: href is referencePhysicalPieceOpen, whose actual definition is the strict physical endpoint interval. Thus href.1.1.trans href.1.2 proves K.physicalLeft j<K.physicalRight j for the same selected j. There is no unjustified global width lower bound.

proof_review.step: Existing genuine affine inverse gives q in unitStrip
proof_review.detail: n07aPhysicalIntervalData K changes only left/right to K.physicalLeft/right. Hence its canonicalOpen is definitionally referencePhysicalPieceOpen S K. n07aCanonicalUnitInversePoint_maps with the same positive width and href gives the displayed literal q in CanonicalGeometry.unitStrip.

proof_review.step: The original point is recovered by physicalUnitPoint
proof_review.detail: n07aCanonicalUnitPoint_inverse supplies canonicalUnitPoint(n07aPhysicalIntervalData K) j q=p. Expanding the actual public project definitions shows this left side is definitionally physicalUnitPoint K j q. Both use K.physicalLeft j+(K.physicalRight j−K.physicalLeft j)*q.1 and retain q.2=p.2. This is the reference physical affine normalization; no equality with a nonlinear current inverseChart is asserted.
